question.question: Can a removed former leader with StepDownOnRemoval=false use the singleton ReadIndex shortcut to certify its old prefix after the surviving voter has independently acquired authority and completed a later write, or does an applicable caller duty or another implementation mechanism exclude that history?
question.importance: A returned stale read certificate could permit a linearizable read to omit a write that completed before the read invocation. This is a possible read safety consequence, not established by the local branch alone.
contexts: Applied joint transition to a singleton retaining a different node
event_paths: Replicated removal -> automatic exit applied -> old leader remains StateLeader -> retained voter campaigns and commits a write -> old node ReadIndex -> caller consumes read state

question.trigger_rationale: Exploration 2b93f866725c4c13ac2c78db651dcb67 executed the full removal/successor history without fabricated protocol state: old node returned index 4 after new node applied index 6. Enabled stepdown returned no certificate. Fix a safety implication so permitted pending behavior is not mistaken for failure.

obligation.description: Under ReadOnlySafe, any returned read-index certificate for a new read must provide a safe log-prefix fence for that read: it must not certify a local prefix excluding a write completed before read invocation in the same Raft history. Removal without immediate stepdown may cause refusal or pending behavior, but must not cause an obsolete former leader to issue a stale safety certificate.

scope.description: Live, unstopped RawNode using ReadOnlySafe and StepDownOnRemoval=false, after actual removal into a different singleton voter configuration; successor write completes before a unique read request on the old node.
assumptions: Caller persists and applies Ready work in order before Advance; no storage failures or crashes.
A write completes only when the retained current voter applies its committed write; read invocation follows that completion.
Read request context is unique; the library node remains unstopped and no embedding-layer read rejection is assumed.
excluded: Applications that stop or reject all reads after local removal.
ReadOnlyLeaseBased, context reuse, early Advance, fabricated terms or progress.
An obligation to return a result when the request is dropped or pending.
Production embedding endpoints, wall-clock deadlines and arbitrary crash recovery.

grounding.derivation: ReadOnlySafe promises linearizable read safety; Node and RawNode ReadIndex describe a returned index as the fence after which prior read requests may safely be processed. In a single log history with a completed write before invocation, a certificate for an earlier prefix cannot suffice when the local application also excludes that write. The API permits lost requests, so the requirement is implication from emitted certificate, not guaranteed success. StepDownOnRemoval is optional and contains no disclaimer weakening ReadOnlySafe when false. The inspected interfaces impose no immediate shutdown or read-rejection duty on removal; Node itself blocks proposals but routes reads independently.
grounding.applicability: Actual removal was committed and applied before the surviving voter campaigns and applies a later write. No higher-term message is forged or suppressed: the new singleton has no reason to send to removed nodes. The old node is queried before periodic quorum loss changes its role, a legal ordering of asynchronous inputs.
alternatives: StepDownOnRemoval=true causes pending/no-certificate behavior in this history and is a valid protection.
Embedding applications may stop removed nodes, limiting exposure; that does not establish protection in the selected live-library scope.
A later CheckQuorum may step down, but future role correction cannot justify an earlier unsafe certificate.

feedback.answered: Exploration reached final singleton membership with old node absent but still StateLeader when stepdown was false. The successor became term-3 leader and applied the write at index 6; only then the old node emitted ReadState index 4 while applied/value remained 4/0. With stepdown enabled no certificate was emitted. This supplies construction knowledge; fixed execution remains separate. The inspected API provides no mandatory immediate-stop duty and preserves ReadOnlySafe independently of the optional removal stepdown.
